title: Agri-Energy Symbiosis: Techno-Economic Feasibility and System Design of an Integrated Aquavoltaic–Seaweed Biodiesel Hub for Rural Energy Autonomy in Bangladesh
content: Bangladesh faces a structural convergence of rural energy and agricultural crises. Diesel fuel — upon which Boro season irrigation entirely depends — reached USD 1.34 per litre in early 2026, while four of five state-owned fertilizer plants remain shuttered due to natural gas shortfalls. Against this backdrop, Bangladesh possesses two substantially underutilised natural assets: approximately 7.1 million hectares of inland water surfaces suitable for floating photovoltaic (FPV) deployment, and abundant coastal stands of the lipid-bearing red macroalga Gracilaria verrucosa with no current commercial energy application. This study proposes and evaluates the "Bio-Solar Hub": a modular, closed-loop agri-energy platform integrating (i) a water-surface FPV electricity array, (ii) an enzymatic seaweed biodiesel micro-refinery powered by the array, and (iii) a bio-fertilizer recovery unit processing the lipid-extraction residue. The study is explicitly a theoretical system design and techno-economic feasibility analysis; no physical prototype was constructed, and all biochemical and engineering parameters are drawn from published peer-reviewed literature. A one-hectare reference farm model is constructed with key parameters: Gracilaria lipid yield at 4.5% dry weight, FPV thermal efficiency advantage of 2.6% over land-mounted panels (water-surface cooling effect), and enzymatic transesterification yield of 90%. Under baseline conditions (25 dry t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ seaweed productivity), the system produces approximately 345 litres of biodiesel and 6,806 kg of bio-fertilizer feedstock annually. The 0.20-ha FPV array generates 537,600 kWh yr⁻¹ at a computed levelised cost of electricity of USD 0.047/kWh — 35% below the national agricultural grid tariff. Over a 25-year project horizon at a 10% discount rate, net present value reaches USD +312,400 with an internal rate of return of 31.7%. Monte Carlo simulation across 5,000 parameter combinations shows the system remains NPV-positive in 97.7% of scenarios. Biodiesel production cost reaches import parity (USD 1.34/L) at 8–12 hectares of cooperative-scale seaweed cultivation. Bio-fertilizer recovery substitutes 32–74% of farm nitrogen requirements across yield scenarios. The Bio-Solar Hub provides a technically coherent, economically competitive pathway toward decentralised energy and fertilizer autonomy for rural Bangladeshi farms.
